title: A PROBLEM NO ONE COULD SOLVE
paragraphs: A PROBLEM NO ONE COULD SOLVE
Pharaoh ruled the most powerful empire of his time.

Gold.
Armies.
Palaces.
Servants waiting for a whisper of his command.

Yet one night…
God gave him a dream that shattered his peace.

Seven fat cows rising from the Nile.
Seven thin cows devouring them.

Seven healthy heads of grain.
Seven scorched heads swallowing the good.

The images were violent.
Disturbing.
Unsettling.
Pharaoh woke up shaken.
And the most powerful man in Egypt suddenly faced a terrifying reality:
He had a problem no one could solve.

He called the magicians.
The advisors.
The experts of Egypt.
The men who claimed to understand mysteries.
But the room filled with silence.

No interpretation.
No answers.
No clarity.
Human wisdom had reached its limit.
And that is exactly where God likes to begin.
Because while Pharaoh was losing sleep in a palace…
Joseph was sleeping in a prison.

Forgotten.
Abandoned by men.
Years stolen by betrayal and injustice.

Sold by his brothers.
Falsely accused.
Locked away.
But heaven had not forgotten him.

What looked like delay…
was actually divine preparation.
While Joseph waited in the darkness, God was building a moment.
A moment so precise that the palace itself would need the man in the prison.
Then suddenly—
The cupbearer remembered.
“Wait… I know someone.”

One memory.
One sentence.
One door opening.
And Joseph was pulled from the pit into the presence of Pharaoh.
But here is what makes the story powerful.
Joseph did not promote himself.
Standing before the most powerful ruler on earth, he said:

“It is not in me; God will give Pharaoh an answer of peace.”
— Genesis 41:16
Read that again.
Joseph had the gift.
Joseph had the insight.
Joseph had the interpretation.
Yet Joseph refused to steal the glory.
Because Joseph knew the truth we often forget:

The answer was never Joseph.
The answer was God.
And in that moment, God did what only He can do.
Joseph interpreted the dream.

Seven years of abundance.
Seven years of devastating famine.
Then Joseph gave the strategy that would save nations.

Grain would be stored.
Lives would be preserved.
Egypt would survive.
But the story is deeper than a dream about cows and grain.
It is a picture of the human condition.
Because humanity also faced a problem no one could solve.
Sin.
A famine of the soul.

No philosophy could fix it.
No religion could erase it.
No human effort could overcome it.
We were trapped.

Guilty.
Broken.
Separated from God.
Then Jesus came.
Not from a palace.
But from humility.

Rejected.
Despised.
Mocked.
Like Joseph, He was betrayed.
Like Joseph, He was falsely condemned.
But unlike Joseph…
Jesus carried the sin of the world.
Where Joseph interpreted a dream that saved people from physical famine…
Jesus became the Bread of Life that saves us from eternal death.
Joseph preserved grain.
Jesus offers salvation.
Joseph saved nations for a season.
Jesus saves souls forever.
And just like Pharaoh needed Joseph to understand the future…
The world desperately needs Christ to understand life itself.
Maybe today you feel like Pharaoh.

Troubled.
Confused.
Searching for answers that nobody seems able to give.
Or maybe you feel like Joseph.

Hidden.
Forgotten.
Wondering if your faithfulness even matters.
Hear this clearly:
God wastes nothing.

Not the prison.
Not the delay.
Not the confusion.
Not the waiting.
God knows how to prepare a moment.

The dream.
The memory.
The opportunity.
The breakthrough.
All timed with divine precision.
And when your moment comes, remember Joseph’s words:
“It is not in me.”
Because the greatest victories in life happen when God gets the glory.
Today the greatest problem humanity ever faced has already been answered.

Not by wisdom.
Not by power.
But by a cross and an empty tomb.
Jesus Christ is the answer.
The Savior.
The Redeemer.
The only One who can forgive sin and give eternal life.
So the question is not whether the answer exists.
The question is whether we will humble ourselves and receive Him.
If you feel like your story is buried in a prison season right now…
Hold on.
God may be preparing a moment that will change everything.
Because the God who raised Joseph from a pit…
is the same God who raised Jesus from the grave.
And that same God is still writing redemption stories today.
“We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.”
📖 Genesis 41
Someone in your circle might be facing a problem they think no one can solve.
But God still has answers. ✝️🔥
